title: Shift cadence & SLO exceptions — weekly check-in
content:
Weekly quick notes — focus this week: stabilize tail latency during promotional traffic spike, smooth shift handoffs, and pilot a small automation to flag SLO drift earlier.

Attendees: Aisha (chair), Evan, Priya, Diego, Marcus (shadow), Lina (observability).

High-level summary:
- Production impact: small but recurring tail-latency blips (~99.9th percentile) during 10:30–12:00 PST window on 9/16 and 9/17. No data loss, some user-facing timeouts for long chaining requests.
- Incident severity: SEV-2 (brief mitigation applied).
- Root cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction storm + model variant fallback thrash on two Dedicated nodes serving mixed seq-length workloads.
- Immediate state: mitigated via manual scaling (add two nodes) and temporarily raising per-request timeout thresholds to reduce cascade.

Incident timeline (sketch):
- 09/16 10:27 PST: first customer reports slow responses from hosted API (large multi-turn requests). Alerts fired: tail-latency SLO > 3x threshold on route /generate-chat.
- 10:30: automated fallback started routing to quantized variant; KV cache churn increased (cache misses x3) and CPU spiky.
- 10:40: on-call applied node scale-up (2 nodes) and toggled routing policy to prefer lower-concurrency lanes for heavy seq requests.
- 11:05: latency improved, alerts cleared.
- 9/17 10:35: similar pattern reappeared; on-call rotated the routing change (longer term fix queued).

SLO snapshot (end of week window):
- Chat-generation route (/generate-chat): availability 99.96% (weekly target 99.99%) — shortfall driven by 9/16 and 9/17 spikes.
- 99th percentile latency: 230 ms (target 200 ms); 99.9th: 1.8 s (target 800 ms).
- Error rate: unchanged (0.03%).
- Observability note: tracing spans missing for some fallback flows — need to expand tracing at the routing layer.

On-call handoff notes (handoff at 2029-09-18 08:00 PST):
- Outgoing: Evan (on-call for night shift) — handoff to Priya.
- Key context for incoming: watch 99.9th for /generate-chat between 10:00–12:00 PST; routing policy flagged INF-3245 contains temporary flag we set to prefer small-batch lanes; do not revert unless latency is below 1s for 30m.
- Access: runbook link in linked_artifacts (Confluence). Credentials for temporary scaling are stored in vault path: vault://redwood/ops/scaling-temp (ask Marcus or SRE lead for one-time token).

Action items / follow-ups (owners + due dates):
- SRE-101: Add detailed tracing to fallback decision path (owner: Priya) — due 2029-09-24.
- SRE-102: Implement a temporary autoscale policy that triggers earlier for high seq-length routers (owner: Diego + infra) — due 2029-09-26.
- SRE-103: Runbook update: add decision matrix for when to route to quantized variants vs add capacity (owner: Aisha) — due 2029-09-21.
- SRE-104: Postmortem draft (short form) for 9/16 & 9/17 incidents (owner: Evan) — due 2029-09-20.
- SRE-105: Create a small Canary test that simulates sustained prefix-heavy sequences to exercise cache behavior in staging (owner: Marcus) — due 2029-09-28.

Tactical mitigations already applied:
- Manual scale + routing preference to reduce mixed-workload contention.
- Raised request timeout limits for 1 hour during peak to reduce downstream cascade.
- Alert thresholds adjusted to reduce alert fatigue for short transient spikes while we investigate root cause.

Risk assessment / priorities this week:
1) Prevent recurrence: medium-high priority (SRE-102 + SRE-101).
2) Improve observability (traces + dashboards) to detect fallback thrash earlier.
3) Decide on a long-term routing policy: prefer static lanes by seq-length or smarter runtime-aware routing.

Notes from standup follow-through: quick wins first:
- Priya will wire a flamegraph sampling for the routing decision microservice to capture CPU pattern during fallback.
- Diego will prototype an early-warning metric (cache-miss-rate * model-fallback-rate) and add an alert with a 5-minute lookback to the stability board.
- Aisha will coordinate a short session with model-ops to discuss quantized variant performance variance; schedule Wed 09/19 14:00 PST.

Handoff checklist (to be confirmed at rotation):
- Verify runbook link and escalation phone list is correct.
- Confirm the temporary scaling token is available or that one-time token flow is understood.
- Ensure postmortem owner is listed and the doc template is created in the SRE folder.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Is the cache eviction pattern driven by sequence-length distribution shift, or by a memory leak in the KV cache expiry policy? Need heap dumps from one Dedicated node during repro window.
- Can we safely move high-seq requests to a separate pool without increasing cost materially? (finance/opportunity cost analysis requested).

Quick links: JIRA SRE-887 (primary), INF-3245 (routing flags), PR #1423 (infra autoscale prototype).

Misc — chatter from the bridge room:
- Customer success noted one premium customer saw a 10% increase in response time on batch jobs; queued to CS sync.
- Observability team will surface a new chart on the dashboard: 'KV cache miss rate by seq-length bucket'.

Closing: goal this week is to stop the recurrence (SRE-102) and get visibility (SRE-101) so we don't have to escalate to Dedicated capacity buys. Keep handoffs thorough — leave route flags explicitly annotated in the runbook.

Raw scratch / quick logs (copied from bridge):
- 2029-09-16-10:31 — alert: /generate-chat - 99.9th 2.3s
- 2029-09-16-10:41 — action: scaled +2 nodes (manual)
- 2029-09-16-11:00 — status: stable
- 2029-09-17-10:38 — alert: same pattern; re-routed
- 2029-09-17-11:15 — status: stable

If you pick this up after handoff, please ping on #sre-ops and add notes to this doc.

-- Aisha
